overview: Perran Beach starts right in Perranporth and runs north-east for about three kilometres to Ligger Point: a vast, wide expanse of sand facing out into Perran Bay. This page is the southern end by the town; the northern part is known as Perran Sands.
With shops, cafés and pubs just behind the beach, this end is an easy family beach day with everything to hand, and because it’s so big you can always find a bit of space.

expect.title: Surf and swimming
expect.text: A popular surfing beach. Lifeguards patrol from May to September; swim between the flags.

expect.title: Room to roam
expect.text: Even in summer, the sheer size of the beach means you can walk away from the busiest bit near town.

expect.title: History in the dunes
expect.text: In the dunes behind, at Penhale Sands, are the remains of St Piran’s Oratory, a 7th-century chapel that lay buried under sand for centuries.

goodToKnow.label: Getting there
goodToKnow.text: Perranporth is around 11 km south-west of Newquay on the B3285, and the coast path passes along the edge of town.

week.slot: Half a day to a full day
week.text: Perranporth makes an easy, low-effort beach day: park, walk onto the sand, and stay as long as you like. If you fancy a stroll, head north along the beach towards Perran Sands, or up onto the cliffs towards St Agnes.

pairWith.why: the wilder northern end of the same beach
a smaller cove at St Agnes
a small free local museum in the village

tips: Walk north along the sand for more space away from the crowds.
At low tide, look out for Chapel Rock and its tidal pool near the town end.
